subject: Surge bucket reservation playbook + MAP for ByteHealth
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@bytehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@bytehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Planning MAP + surge buckets — timing and lead times

Marcus — thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have agreement from the exec team to move toward a dedicated/private capacity plan but need to fold this into a tight MAP. High level asks:

- We expect a pilot of ~100 concurrent sessions (avg 1.2k tokens/session) ramping to 500 concurrent over 3 months.
- Primary requirement: predictable p95 latency < 300ms for generation paths.
- Timing constraint: procurement needs a clear lead time and a PO-ready cost estimate by Apr 9 to hit our Q2 launch.

Can you share a mutual action plan template that maps evaluation milestones to reservation tranches and a GPU sizing recommendation (including H100 vs A100 tradeoffs)? Also need SOC2 evidence snippets — procurement will ask.

Attachments: — I can share our internal traffic-profile.csv if useful.

Thanks,
Helen Park
VP Product, ByteHealth
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@bytehealth.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@bytehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning MAP + surge buckets — timing and lead times

Helen — great to hear the exec thumbs up. I attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet (ByteHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx) that breaks the plan into three tranches: pilot (small), scale-bridge, and committed pool. The sheet includes recommended GPU counts for each tranche using two sizing profiles (throughput optimized on H100 and cost-optimized on quantized A100). I also included a one-pager SOC2 summary (SOC2_summary.pdf) and a CSV with our current H100 lead-time estimates (h100-leadtime-estimates.csv).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- You and Samir review the sizing table and confirm target concurrency/latency expectations by Tue 4/6.
- Internal call (30m) between ByteHealth + Redwood to finalize MAP milestones and acceptance criteria on Wed 4/7.
- Once milestones are agreed, Redwood will return a PO-ready commitment schedule and pricing by Fri 4/9.

Notes on lead times: H100 capacity options show potential lead windows of 8–12 weeks for dedicated pools in our current procurement lanes; A100 (quantized) options can be provisioned faster (2–4 weeks) but with additional SLO tuning required. The MAP includes a fallback lane that routes traffic to a reserved shared pool during the H100 ramp.

Attachment: ByteHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — main tab: MAP schedule; tabs: sizing_profiles, acceptance_criteria, financials.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ByteHealth MAP draft — sizing sanity check

Looping in sizing/ops: I reviewed the MAP_v1 and have two immediate flags:

1) Pilot tranche shows 12 x H100 (smaller multi-instance) — that seems high given their stated token distribution. If they run smaller batches we should push a mixed H100/A100 bridge instead of full H100 for pilot.

2) Acceptance criteria: we need clear eval prompts and a gate for QoQ latency regressions. Add a prompt-set tab and tie the regression alert thresholds into the canary step. Procurement will ask for the exact pass/fail metrics.

Action items for Marcus/Karthik:
- Karthik: can you add quantization recommendation rows (LLM-optim vs dynamic) and expected cost delta by tranche?
- Priyom: can ops pre-validate the H100 lane lead times and confirm any potential accelerated delivery options (e.g., priority procurement) by EOD today so we can keep the Apr 9 PO target.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ByteHealth MAP draft — sizing sanity check

Thanks Marissa — quick notes inline:

- Quantization: recommend int8+LLM-optim for the A100 bridge; expect ~40% cost reduction vs baseline fp16 H100 with ~5–8% latency increase under peak. Put numbers in a new tab (done).
- H100 lead times: Priyom ran the procurement lane; typical is 8–11 weeks but we can sometimes compress to 6 weeks using our marketplace partner (fee applies).
- Suggested MAP change: split the ‘scale-bridge’ into two mini tranches so we can decouple acceptance gating from the full committed pool cutover. That helps procurement align PO tranches to vendor lead windows.

I updated ByteHealth_MAP_v1.xlsx with quant rows and a split-bridge timeline. Marcus — please review the updated tab before sending to Helen.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Helen Park <helen.park@bytehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir@bytehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Planning MAP + surge buckets — timing and lead times

Team — this looks good and aligns to our procurement windows. A couple of points from procurement:

- We can accept a two-tranche PO (pilot tranche + scale commitment) if you provide a PO-ready pricing schedule and a clear rollback/fallback (shared pool) in case H100 arrives later than the compressed lead estimate.
- Please include an explicit latency acceptance test (p95 < 300ms over 30m sustained traffic) and a prompt-set for evaluation.

If you can send the updated MAP (with the split-bridge and quantization rows) and a PO-ready schedule by EOD 4/6 we will route to procurement for signature on 4/9. Otherwise we may need to buy a short-term shared-pool bridge externally which complicates the cost profile.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Helen
Helen Park
VP Product, ByteHealth
